MS1Match

MS1Match is an R package for library-guided, compound-centric grouping and annotation of redundant LC-MS features. It uses full-range MS1 and MS2 reference libraries to assign adducts, multimers, isotopes, neutral losses and in-source fragments to the compounds they originate from.

Main functions:

  1. Preprocessing (optional): feature detection from raw data with the xcms framework, or import of feature tables from MZmine or CSV files
  2. Library matching: direct matching of detected features to MS1 and MS2 reference spectra
  3. Feature annotation with evidence tiers: ion type, isotopologue, MS2 fragment and neutral-loss evidence (Tiers 1a to 1d), plus matched but unexplained features (Tier 2)
  4. M-expansion: extension of each compound group to co-eluting features without a direct library match (expansion tiers)
  5. Evaluation of grouping tools: reference-relative comparison of other feature grouping tools (e.g., CAMERA, RAMClustR) against the compound-centric MS1Match groups

Overview

Installation

Requirements

  • R >= 4.5, with the matching Bioconductor release
  • Rcpp: required (the package contains compiled C++ code)
  • Build tools to compile the C++ code:

    • Windows: Rtools matching your R version (R 4.5.x → Rtools45)

    • macOS: Apple Command Line Tools

      xcode-select --install

    • Linux (Ubuntu/Debian):

      sudo apt update
sudo apt install build-essential r-base-dev
install.packages("Rcpp")

Bioconductor dependencies 

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install(
  c("xcms", "MSnbase", "Spectra", "MetaboCoreUtils",
    "MsExperiment", "MsBackendMgf", "BiocParallel", "S4Vectors"),
  ask = FALSE, update = TRUE
)

Optional, only for the tool comparisons in tutorial 3:

BiocManager::install("CAMERA")
install.packages("RAMClustR")

Install MS1Match 

if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github("RuibingS/MS1Match_Rpackage",
                        build_vignettes = TRUE,
                        dependencies    = TRUE)

build_vignettes = TRUE knits the tutorials during installation, which takes a few minutes. Leave it out for a faster install; the tutorials are then not available offline with vignette().

Check the installation 

library(MS1Match)
packageVersion("MS1Match")
browseVignettes("MS1Match")

Troubleshooting

  • Permission denied on a .dll (Windows): the package is loaded in an R session and its DLL is locked. Restart R (Session → Restart R in RStudio), close other R sessions, and install again before loading any package.
  • “… dependencies are out of date”: a notice, not an error. To skip updating them, add upgrade = "never" to install_github().
  • A Bioconductor package fails to install: check that the R and Bioconductor versions match with BiocManager::valid().

Using Docker

A Dockerfile is provided to run the package in a reproducible environment without installing the dependencies manually.

1. Clone the repository 

git clone https://github.com/RuibingS/MS1Match_Rpackage.git
cd MS1Match_Rpackage

2. Build the Docker image 

docker build -t ms1match .

3. Run an interactive R session 

docker run -it --rm ms1match
  • -it opens an interactive terminal for the R console
  • --rm removes the container after you exit R (q())

Inside the container:

library(MS1Match)

Optional: mount a local folder

To work with files from your computer:

docker run -it --rm -v "$(pwd)":/workspace ms1match

This mounts the current directory at /workspace inside the container. On Windows (PowerShell), use -v "${PWD}:/workspace".

Tutorials

The tutorials follow the three steps of a typical analysis. Each one starts from the output of the previous one, so you can enter wherever your data already are.

raw files ──> [1] xcms ──> feature table ──> [2] MS1Match ──> anno_result ──> [3] evaluate a grouping tool
              (optional)                     (StM14 / SuperPool)              (CAMERA, RAMClustR, any tool)
# Tutorial What it covers Start here if you have
1 Preprocessing with xcms Peak picking, alignment and correspondence (runxcmsFT() or step by step); export of the feature table Raw .mzML / .mzXML files
2a MS1Match workflow: StM14 Main tutorial. 14 standards spiked into a P. aeruginosa extract, MS1 + MS2: consensus MS2 spectra, direct library match, Phase 1 / Phase 2 annotation, in-source fragments, tier summary, export An xcms feature table
2b MS1Match workflow: SuperPool The same workflow on a pooled sample of MSMLS standards and a larger in-house library An xcms feature table (larger example)
2c Other inputs: MZmine, CSV, no MS2 MS1Match on an MZmine full feature table (read_mzmine_feature_table()) or any CSV (read_feature_table()), without MS2; evaluating MZmine’s own groupings A feature table from MZmine or other software
3 Evaluate a grouping tool Benchmarking CAMERA, RAMClustR, MZmine or any other tool against the MS1Match reference set: standard grouping table, same-feature-table check, tier-stratified results An anno_result and a grouping result from the same feature table

After installation, the same tutorials are available offline:

browseVignettes("MS1Match")
vignette("02a_ms1match_StM14", package = "MS1Match")

Which path do I follow?

  • Starting from raw files: 1 → 2a → (3)
  • Feature table from xcms: 2a → (3)
  • Feature table from MZmine, MS-DIAL or a CSV: 2c → (3)
  • Benchmarking a grouping tool and you already have anno_result: 3 only

Tutorial 3 never runs MS1Match itself. It reuses the anno_result and the feature table from tutorial 2, so the grouping tool must have been run on the same feature table. Tutorial 3 shows how to check this.

Example data

All tutorials run on example data shipped in inst/extdata. Slow steps (peak picking, MS2 consensus building) are loaded from cached .rds files; the code to recompute them from raw files is included but not run.

Dataset Content Library
StM14 14 standards spiked into a P. aeruginosa metabolome extract at three concentrations, MS1 + DDA MS2 Si14 (14 compounds)
StM14 (MZmine) The same samples processed with MZmine 3: full feature table of the 9 MS1 files, with MZmine’s correlation groups and ion identity networks Si14 (14 compounds)
SuperPool Pooled MSMLS standards, MS1 + DDA MS2 CBIO in-house library, restricted to the pool’s targets

Analyses for the manuscript

The analysis/ folder holds the full benchmark analyses reported in the manuscript: CAMERA and RAMClustR evaluations on StM14 and SuperPool. All Ref-* counts come from evaluate_grouping(), the same function as in tutorial 3; the CAMERA files add adduct-annotation accuracy, confusion analysis and case studies. They are not built as vignettes. Render them with rmarkdown::render() after installing the package; the knitted reports are in analysis/html/.

File Content
analysis/StM14_CAMERA_evaluation.Rmd CAMERA pcgroups vs. the MS1Match reference set: tier benchmark, pcgroup purity, adduct annotation coverage / accuracy, failure-cause analysis, compound case studies
analysis/StM14_RAMClustR_evaluation.Rmd The same grouping evaluation for RAMClustR, with coverage and cluster purity per compound
analysis/SuperPool_CAMERA_evaluation.Rmd The CAMERA evaluation on SuperPool
analysis/SuperPool_RAMClustR_evaluation.Rmd The RAMClustR evaluation on SuperPool
